# Changelog

All notable changes to RoomKit are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **`ThinkingDeltaMarker` is public, from `roomkit.models`** (RMK-1021). A
  streaming channel's `deliver_stream` reads one per chunk of the model's
  reasoning, besides the text and the response's rows, and could name it
  only through an internal module. `Channel.deliver_stream` now annotates
  its stream `AsyncIterator[str | ThinkingDeltaMarker | RoomEvent]`, what it
  carried already; an override typed `AsyncIterator[str]` widens to it.

- **`MCPToolProvider.from_command(..., connect_timeout=60.0)`** (RMK-1021,
  as roomkit-rs's `McpCommand`). Entering a provider that starts its server
  waited for the handshake and the listing for ever: a server that never
  answered held its host. Entering now takes `connect_timeout` seconds at
  most, the start, the handshake and the listing together; past it the
  server is stopped and entering raises `TimeoutError`. The constructor
  takes it too, for stdio only (`ValueError` on an HTTP transport).

- **`pause_room()`, `resume_room()` and `reopen_room()`** (RFC 5.1,
  RMK-1021). The RFC names the three transitions and roomkit-rs has them;
  a host could only close or archive a room. A pause fires
  `ON_ROOM_PAUSED` and emits no `room_paused`, which reports the timer's;
  a resume and a reopen report nothing and restart the inactivity timer.
  A transition already done does nothing; one from a status it does not
  leave from raises `TransitionRefusedError`, nothing written (a reopen of
  a room that is not CLOSED among them).
- **`ConversationStore.delete_participant(room_id, participant_id)`** (RFC
  14.1, RMK-1021), in every store. **BREAKING** for a store written outside
  RoomKit: the method is abstract.

- **`roomkit.testing`: a transport that records what it is handed, and an
  agent that echoes** (RMK-1021). A test or an example saw a room work
  through a channel of its own; roomkit-rs's examples and tests use the
  same two from `roomkit::testing`.
  - `RecordingTransport(channel_id, channel_type, *, capabilities=None)`
    records every event delivered to it: `deliveries` holds each as a
    `Delivery(event, text)`, `texts` the texts alone. It needs no
    recipient and addresses its senders as its type does.
  - `EchoAgent(channel_id, reply, *, quote=False)` answers every event it
    is asked with `reply`, followed by the event's text when `quote` is set.
  - `examples/testing_channels.py` shows both.

- **A tool call's intent: the sentence the model writes for the person with
  each call** (RFC 6.4, RMK-1040). `AIChannel(..., tool_call_intents=True)`
  shows each tool's schema with the optional `_roomkit_intent` property; the
  tool loop takes it out of the call's arguments before the gate and carries
  it, normalized, as `intent` on `ToolCallEvent`, on the `TOOL_CALL_START` and
  `TOOL_CALL_END` ephemeral events and on `ToolCallContent`.
  - The handler, `BEFORE_TOOL_USE` and the schema check see the tool's own
    arguments: a closed schema no longer refuses the call over the property.
  - A missing or unusable intent is `None` and never fails a call; a tool
    whose schema declares the property keeps it as its argument.
  - Off by default: schemas, arguments, events and rows are unchanged. A row
    or a turn frame carries `intent` only when it has one.
  - `AIToolCall` and `StreamToolCall` gain `intent`. Realtime sessions, ACP
    agents and provider-served calls carry none; an agent a realtime session
    delegates to takes the property out but reports through the session,
    without it.

- **`KitClosedError` and `ShutdownCancelledError`, both `RoomKitError`s**
  (RFC 12.10.4, RMK-1030).
  - `KitClosedError` is what a closing kit raises to a call that writes or
    delivers, and to every other call but a read or a teardown call; it is
    also the code (`kit_closed`) of a send its close cut. It replaces the
    plain `RoomKitError` a call met after the store was sealed, or a
    delegation or a strategy's run asked for on a closing kit.
  - `ShutdownCancelledError` is what `close()` raises to a caller nobody
    cancelled once the shutdown itself was cut (every task cancelled, as
    `asyncio.run` does as it ends). It used to be a plain `RoomKitError`.

- **`SystemOneClassifier` asks a decision model on any server with a
  System One API** (RFC 6.8, RMK-1025). TypeSafe's API (`POST
  {base_url}/v1/systemone`) is now also served by Ollama (d3, d1, nimble,
  tev1, clef…), a LiteLLM proxy (Jev, OpenAI's Decisions models translated,
  Clef…), llama.cpp and vLLM.
  - `SystemOneClassifier(base_url, model=..., api_key=None)` asks any of
    them through the TypeSafe SDK (`roomkit[typesafe]`). The model is
    required, since the SDK's default is a TypeSafe one.
  - It was probed against TypeSafe, LiteLLM to Jev and to `gpt-6-luna`,
    Ollama with `d3:2b` and `d1:2b`, and llama.cpp with d1.
  - A score is the expected level, computed from each level's probability:
    llama.cpp sent the likeliest level in its `score` field instead.
- **`LlamaCppClassifier` runs a decision model itself through llama.cpp**
  (RMK-1025), the way `LlamaCppAIProvider` runs a chat model.
  `LlamaCppClassifier(LlamaCppConfig(model="LiquidAI/d1-2B-GGUF:Q8_0"))`
  downloads llama.cpp and the model, starts `llama-server`, and stops it on
  `close()`. It needs the `typesafe` and `llamacpp` extras.

### Changed

- **BREAKING — a store refuses a participant under an id its room has**
  (RFC 5.5, 14.3; RMK-1021), as roomkit-rs's `ParticipantExists`.
  `add_participant()` replaced the record the room held, in the three
  stores; a participant is one record per room and id. It now raises
  `ParticipantExistsError`, exported from `roomkit`, and keeps the record.
  The kit's own paths read the record first, under the room lock, and are
  unchanged; a host that called the store's `add_participant()` to rewrite
  a record calls `update_participant()`.

- **`ConversationStore.get_timeline()` reads 50 events by default**, as
  `RoomKit.get_timeline()` and roomkit-rs's `EventQuery` (RMK-1021). The one
  name had two defaults, 100 on the store and 50 on the kit. A caller of the
  store's read that relied on 100 passes `limit=100`.

- **BREAKING — a store implements `commit_event()` and
  `advance_delivered_index()` itself** (RFC 14.1, 14.3; RMK-1021). The base
  class gave both a default that read, then wrote, in separate steps: a
  concurrent writer, in this process or another, could see an event without
  its room's counters, index two events alike, or move the delivery cursor
  past one index twice. Both are now abstract, as in roomkit-rs's `Store`;
  the shipped stores already implemented each in one transaction. A store
  written outside RoomKit that inherited them no longer instantiates:
  implement `commit_event()` as one transaction (the event, the room's
  `event_count` and `latest_index`, the target of an edit or a delete), and
  `advance_delivered_index()` as one conditional write.

- **BREAKING — no channel of the type `SYSTEM`, and no empty id**
  (RFC 5, 6.2, 10.3; RMK-1021).
  - `register_channel()` refuses a channel of the type `SYSTEM`
    (`ValueError`): the type is the framework's own records', whose source
    may make the changes reserved to the system. A SYSTEM edit or delete
    now comes from a hook (an injected event), the one door left for it.
  - A room's, a channel's, an event's, a participant's and an identity's
    id is never empty: the models raise `ValidationError` for `""`, and
    `create_room(room_id="")` raises instead of making up an id.

- **A channel type is an open name** (RFC 6.2, RMK-986). An integrator's
  channel for a platform the enum does not list (Slack, Signal, Line) had to
  pick a wrong type, such as `WEBHOOK`, and lost the addressing its own
  should give. `ChannelType("slack")` is now a type: any name of lowercase
  ASCII letters, digits, `_` and `-`, read and written back as it is, the
  same each time; another name raises `ValueError`. The members stay, as
  the well-known names. A channel declares its addressing
  (`TransportChannel(..., addressing=ChannelAddressing(...))`), its
  well-known name's by default, as written for any other.

- **BREAKING — four values are checked as roomkit-rs checks them**
  (RMK-1021, decision 19 of the API parity work).
  - `EditContent.edit_source` is an `EditSource` (`sender`, `system`) or
    none, so any other value raises `ValidationError` as the edit is built.
    It was read as the sender's (RFC 10.3); an id written there, as old
    examples did, now has to go.
  - A country code given to `TransportChannel(country_code=...)` or to
    `ChannelAddressing.normalize()` is one to three digits, the first not
    0, with or without its `+`; another raises `ValueError`. `"0x"` left
    every national number unchanged, the mistake unseen.
  - A `ToolPolicy` pattern, and a skill's `allowed_tools` and `requires`,
    read `*` and `?` alone (RFC 21.1), and a pattern holding `[` or `]` is
    refused: `ValueError` for a `ToolPolicy` or a `RoleOverride`,
    `SkillValidationError` for a skill. `look[uv]p` allowed `lookup`;
    read as written, `deny=["rm_[a-z]*"]` would have let `rm_file`
    through, so a rule written as a character class now fails where it
    is configured. A skill's `[ab]` reads as the list it is, gating `ab`.
  - The skills' manifest, which every system prompt carries, stays within
    65,536 characters (RFC 24.1): a discovery, a registration or an `add`
    that would pass it raises `SkillManifestTooLargeError`, a
    `SkillError`, and registers nothing.
- **`channel_data` keeps the keys its channel writes** (RFC 5.4, RMK-1021).
  `ChannelData` dropped every key it did not name (an SMS's `segments`, an
  email's `subject`); they are now kept on the event and in the store.

- **An event's ASYNC hooks no longer hold its call or its room** (RFC 9.3,
  RMK-1020). An event's `AFTER_BROADCAST` hooks, the `ON_EVENT_UPDATED` or
  `ON_EVENT_DELETED` of an edit or a delete, `ON_TASK_CREATED` and an
  agent's `ON_ERROR` ran in the room's delivery lane: `process_inbound`
  returned only once they had ended, a room's hooks ran one after the
  other, and the room's next message and an agent's answer waited behind
  them, so a 1 s audit hook added 1 s to every reply. They now run on tasks
  of their own, as roomkit-rs runs them.
  - The call returns once its delivery set and its answers are done: a
    caller that reads a hook's effect right after it returns may not see it
    yet. `event_processed` still comes once the event's `AFTER_BROADCAST`
    hooks have ended.
  - Each body still draws on its cascade's budget and depth, so a hook that
    posts after every event still stops at the cap, and `kit.close()` still
    gives them the grace, then cuts them. A call no longer reads `kit_closed`
    for its hook alone.
  - An `AFTER_BROADCAST` hook that sends, then closes the kit: its send is
    dropped as the close starts, as before, whatever the store; another
    call's send under way gets the grace, then is cut, as any send.

- **A room change no longer waits for its ASYNC hooks** (RFC 9.3,
  RMK-1020). `attach_channel`, `detach_channel`, `mute`, `unmute`,
  `close_room`, `check_room_timers`, `add_member`, `remove_member`,
  `rename_member`, a conference's participant and track announcements, and
  a direct `update_event` or `delete_event` returned only once their hooks
  had ended: a 1 s hook on `ON_CHANNEL_ATTACHED` made every attach take
  1 s. They now start the hooks and return, as roomkit-rs does.
  - A caller that reads a hook's effect right after the call may not see
    it yet; `kit.hook_engine.drain_observers()` waits for the hooks still
    running.
  - `create_room` still awaits its `ON_ROOM_CREATED` hooks: one that
    attaches the room's agent has done so before anything is sent into the
    room.
  - A direct change's hooks still run on the budget of the work it is made
    in, so a hook that edits its event on every edit still stops at the
    cap; `kit.close()` gives them the grace, then cuts them, and no longer
    cuts the timer check that started them.

- **The triggers only Python has no longer wait for their ASYNC hooks**
  (RFC 9.3, RMK-1049). An agent's answer waited for its `ON_AI_RESPONSE`
  hooks, `submit_feedback` for `ON_FEEDBACK`'s, `process_delivery_status`
  for `ON_DELIVERY_STATUS`'s, a delegation for `ON_TASK_DELEGATED`'s and
  `ON_TASK_COMPLETED`'s, a recording's stop for `ON_RECORDING_STOPPED`'s;
  so did `ON_STATUS_POSTED`, `ON_PROTOCOL_TRACE`, `ON_SPEAK_QUEUE`,
  `ON_DISPATCH_DECISION`, `ON_HANDOFF`, `AFTER_DELIVER`, the identity
  observers and the turn observers. They now start the hooks and go on.
  - The framework event that reports the operation (`ai_response`,
    `feedback`, `recording_started`, `recording_stopped`) still comes once
    its hooks have ended, as `event_processed` does.
  - Two more awaited exceptions, beside `ON_ROOM_CREATED`, unchanged:
    `ON_RECORDING_STARTED`, the consent point no media reaches a recording
    before, and the triggers of a voice, realtime, conference or video
    session's stream (speech edges, partials, barge-in, turns, DTMF,
    `AFTER_TTS`...), observed in order with the stream's next trigger, so
    a partial transcription never lands after its final.
  - A task's line on the status bus reads ended as its `ON_TASK_COMPLETED`
    hooks start, no longer once they end. The discussion console names a
    task's owner whichever of its start and its tool call it hears first.

- **`LlamaCppAIProvider` runs llama.cpp's latest stable release, v0.8.0
  (build b11960)** (RMK-1024).
  - The pinned build was b11160, a nightly from September. It could not
    load the models llama.cpp added since, LiquidAI LFM3 among them.
  - `LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B-GGUF:Q4_K_M` now runs from its Hugging Face
    reference, its tool calls right on GPU and CPU.
  - Keep its reasoning on (`enable_thinking` left `None`). With it off, the
    model writes `answer</think>answer`, and llama.cpp leaves that in the
    reply.
  - `make update-llamacpp` pins the latest stable release by default
    instead of the newest nightly; `BUILD=v0.8.0` or `BUILD=b11960` names
    one.

- **An AI channel's earlier tool calls ride its history as tool messages**
  (RFC 6.4, RMK-1023). From one turn to the next, the tools an agent called
  were recalled in a "Tools you've already used here" block. That block was
  added to the turn's notes, which ride the participant's last message.
  Models answered that block as if the participant had asked for it: after a
  booking, a "Hi there!" got the booking restated. That happened 7 times in
  10 on gpt-6-luna and 10 in 10 on LFM3-1.7B.
  - Each round of an earlier turn now reads, at its place in the history,
    as the assistant's calls then their results, the way the turn itself
    sent them. The same measure gives 0 in 10 on both models, with the same
    recall of the results.
  - The rounds are read from the store every turn, the channel's own calls
    only. The bounds stay those of the block it replaces: the last 8 calls,
    the 3 most recent with their result whole up to 6000 characters (less
    under a low eviction threshold), the older ones as a preview.
  - A refused call is still left out.
  - A result evicted in its turn replays as the placeholder the model read
    then, which the re-read tool serves while the room still stores it. The
    block used to give the next turn the first 6000 characters of the
    result itself. Once the stored copy is gone (a restart), the result
    reads as its size alone, as before.
  - The turn's notes no longer carry the block. Tool Search still re-reveals
    the tools already used, and the latest images their results returned
    still ride the input.

- **BREAKING — once `kit.close()` starts, every call but a read or a
  teardown call raises `KitClosedError`** (RFC 12.10.4, RMK-1030). A closing
  kit took calls until its store was sealed, so traffic kept the close open
  and a call made in the close's last moments was stored and never
  delivered. Now admission stops as `close()` starts, whoever calls: an
  outside caller, a hook or a tool still running, a channel's own `close()`.
  - Refused: every call that writes or delivers, and every other one too,
    synchronous calls included: `steer`, `transcribe`, `synthesize`,
    `delegate`, `register_channel`, `unregister_channel`, `hook()`, `on()`,
    `identity_hook()`, `on_delivery_status()`, `subscribe_websocket`,
    `setup_background`, `setup_task_tools`… A channel's own doors refuse
    the same way: `RealtimeVoiceChannel.start_session`, a participant
    arriving in a conference (quietly, at debug). `async with` on a closed
    kit raises it too. `commit_event` after the close no longer writes.
  - The reads (`get_room`, `get_timeline`, `get_binding`, `list_*`,
    `is_member`, `regenerate_target`, `room_recordings`,
    `room_strategy_is_current`, `sender_verification`, `source_health`,
    `verification_of`, and the synchronous `get_channel`, `hooks_for`,
    `identity_enabled_for`, `list_channels`, `list_sources`,
    `room_strategy`, `speak_queue`) answer during the close, and after it
    while the store is open: an `InMemoryStore`, or a Postgres pool the
    integrator handed in. A store the kit closed (SQLite, a Postgres pool
    the kit opened) refuses them with `KitClosedError`, never its own
    error. Work a read starts (a source's health check) is no read.
  - The teardown calls return doing nothing, since the close tears down
    what they would: `cancel_delivery` (0), `cancel_task` (False),
    `disconnect_websocket`, `disconnect_voice`, `disconnect_video`, `leave`,
    `unsubscribe_websocket` (None), `unsubscribe_room` (False).
  - A call under way when the close starts reads `kit_closed` in its
    `cancellation_reason`, even when its sends end within the grace.

  Migration: let a hook or a channel's close that may run during a close
  catch `KitClosedError`. A read after the close on a store the kit closed
  raises `KitClosedError`: catch it, not the store's `RuntimeError`.

- **BREAKING — `kit.close()` no longer drains: what has not started is cut
  at once, the running work gets one grace of 5 s** (RFC 12.10.4,
  RMK-1030).
  - A delivery queued in a room's lane behind another is dropped at once,
    never sent; it used to be delivered if the lane's 5 s drain reached it.
    One placed in an idle lane runs from its placement (RMK-1039). The
    kit's background runs and its verification timers are cut at once too.
  - A call waiting for its room's lock is cut at once, nothing of it
    stored: `process_inbound` and `regenerate_response` return
    `InboundResult(blocked=True, reason="kit_closed")`, `send_event`,
    `commit_event` and a room change (`attach_channel`,
    `update_room_metadata`, `close_room`…) raise `KitClosedError`. It used
    to wait for the lock, then fail on the sealed store after `close()` had
    returned.
  - A call whose hooks or commit outlast the grace is cut the same way. One
    whose commit had started when it was cut reads its event back once its
    writes unwound, within the unwind: stored, `process_inbound` returns
    it as `InboundResult.event` with `cancellation_reason="kit_closed"`
    (a BLOCKED record keeping its hooks' reason), and `send_event`,
    `commit_event` and `post` return it, never a refusal. A store that
    completes the write after that, or a read-back that fails (logged as a
    warning), leaves the call reported as not stored.
  - A call that commits within the grace is stored, and delivered to no
    one: its delivery is dropped as the queued ones are, its
    `delivery_results` empty.
  - A hook, a store write, a room change or a transport send still running
    gets one grace of 5 s from the close's start, then is cut. A write is
    no longer waited for on 5 s, again on the same deadline, then on a
    fresh 5 s after the channels closed, and left running past that. The
    kit's own steps that wait on integrator code (a source's `stop()`, a
    delegation's `on_complete`) run side by side within the same grace, so
    a slow one holds no other back, each logging its own failure as it
    ends, and every source's task is cut, whatever its `stop()` does; a
    source restarting on failure is not restarted once the close started. The handlers a voice or video
    channel runs for a session's start or end get the grace too. What a
    channel's close starts is cut at once.
  - The close takes the grace, plus the turn backend's close (its turns and
    the calls they made, cut and waited for one unwind, 1 s, in process, and
    its cancel bound, `TurnTimeouts.cancel`, across Redis), plus the
    channels' closes and the kit's own backends' closes (voice, realtime,
    the store, the lock managers, the status bus), each on its own budget,
    plus at most 1 s more, twice: after the grace and after the channels,
    for cut work that ignores its cancellation. The operations the store or
    the lock manager still runs are waited for within the second one. The
    kit's close gives the connections still in use of a pool a
    `PostgresStore` or a `PostgresAdvisoryLockManager` opened 1 s to come
    back, then terminates them; their own `close()`, called by their owner,
    waits for them as before, and a pool handed in stays its owner's. With
    a send, a write, an observer and a hook that never end, it took 19.8 s;
    it takes 5 s.
  - Nothing is written or delivered after `close()` returns by work that
    honours its cut. Work that ignores it past the unwind is abandoned and
    named in one line of the log, each task by the work it runs (a source's
    stop, a turn): a store the kit closed then refuses its
    writes, a store that stays open (an `InMemoryStore`, a pool handed in)
    takes them, and a send it still makes is its channel's own.

  Migration: for a delivery that must go out, wait for
  `result.delivery.wait()` before `close()`.

- **BREAKING — `kit.close()` cuts a model turn at once** (RFC 12.10.4,
  RMK-1030). A turn in progress, its stream and its tool calls, is cut as
  the close starts, while the other running work has its grace. It used to
  be cut only once every lane had drained, up to 6 s later. What it
  streamed is stored marked `cancelled`, and an open tool call gets its end
  row, `failed`, error `kit_closed`. The turn a tool closing the kit runs
  in is cut the same way, but the call that awaits `close()` itself runs
  on: its end row is stored before the kit releases its store, and what the
  turn does after the close is refused quietly, no error logged. A call
  that awaits a close it started on a task of its own is cut with its turn,
  and the close runs on. Migration: let a turn whose answer you need end
  before `close()`.

- **`TurnExecutor.close()` spares the task it is called from** (RFC
  12.10.4, RMK-1030). A close called from inside one of the executor's
  turns used to cut its own caller along with the rest. It now leaves that
  task to run, as the kit's close does. When the owner then cuts a turn the
  close spared, that turn ends for its owner at once and stops watching it;
  it used to run on and keep speaking to its owner. A close called from
  outside every turn behaves as before.

- **BREAKING — a call `kit.close()` cuts reads `kit_closed`, never
  `lane_cancelled`, with what it delivered** (RFC 12.10.4, RMK-1030). A
  close gave `lane_cancelled` to the deliveries its lane's round had taken
  and `kit_closed` to the ones queued, all with empty `delivery_results`.
  Every call it cuts now reads `cancellation_reason == "kit_closed"`, its
  answers already stored, and each target's delivery: a target delivered
  keeps `sent`, a send cut mid-way, or one that ignored its cut, is
  `failed` with code `kit_closed`, retryable. A deferred call's
  `delivery.wait()` returns once its delivery set ended or was cut, no
  longer as the close starts. `lane_cancelled` is no longer given by a
  close. Migration: read `kit_closed` where a close gave `lane_cancelled`.

- **BREAKING — a `kit.close()` after one that failed raises the same
  failure** (RFC 12.10.4, RMK-1015). A channel that fails to close makes
  `close()` raise an `ExceptionGroup`; a later `close()` used to return
  without a word, as if the kit had closed cleanly. It now raises that same
  `ExceptionGroup`, as a channel's own `close()` does: the kit's close
  reports what its one shutdown achieved, and never runs it again. The exit
  of an `async with RoomKit()` block is such a later call. Migration: a
  failed `close()` called and handled inside `async with RoomKit()` is
  raised again by the block's exit; drop that call and handle the failure
  around the block.

- **An ASYNC `BEFORE_BROADCAST` hook starts once its event's pass is
  over: the event stored and its delivery placed in the room's lane** (RFC
  9.2, 10.1, RMK-1039). It started as the SYNC hooks ended, before the
  commit. On a store whose commit waits on its I/O (SQLite, Postgres), it
  then ran while the event was being written: an observer reading the
  store could miss its event, and one that closed the kit made the close
  drop the event's own delivery, placed after the close started, where an
  `InMemoryStore` delivered it. It now starts as its pass ends, on every
  store and every pass: a message, a `send_event`, a `post`, an agent's
  answer or a regenerated one, a channel's response, a hook's injected
  event. It still observes the event as the SYNC hooks left it, in the
  same context, and an event they blocked still has none. As before, one
  they allowed is observed even when its pass then ends without storing
  it as sent: its source may not write (stored `BLOCKED`), the room closed
  or an edit's target was refused meanwhile, `process_timeout` ran out, or
  the commit failed. A pass the kit's close cuts before its commit ended
  now starts none (RMK-1046), as in roomkit-rs: nothing new starts once
  the close began, where its observers started and were then refused or
  cut.

### Fixed

- **A store refuses a write naming what it lacks** (RFC 14.3, RMK-1021),
  as roomkit-rs's stores. `update_event()` of an event the store does not
  hold raises `EventNotFoundError`: the memory store kept it as a row no
  timeline read found, SQLite raised an `IntegrityError` or kept it, and
  Postgres wrote nothing without a word. `add_participant()` into a room the
  store does not hold raises `RoomNotFoundError`: the memory and SQLite
  stores kept a participant of no room, and Postgres raised asyncpg's
  `ForeignKeyViolationError`. Nothing is written in either case.

- **`list_events(before_index=..., limit=0)` returns no event** on the
  memory store (RMK-1021), as the other stores and every other window: it
  returned the whole window below the cursor.

- **`check_all_timers()` reaches every room** (RMK-1009). A sweep read one
  page of rooms per status, the store's 100 by default, so past the first
  100 ACTIVE and 100 PAUSED rooms no timer ever paused or closed a room. It
  now reads every page before it checks any room.

- **A close from an observer on an agent's answer logs nothing** (RFC
  12.10.4, RMK-1043). The answer's row keeps the end its commit carried;
  the turn wrote that end again as the kit closed, which refused it, and a
  WARNING with a traceback came on an ordinary close. The refused rewrite
  is now skipped quietly, as roomkit-rs does.

- **A `BEFORE_TOOL_USE` MODIFY serves the call** (RFC 9.3, RMK-1021). The
  next hook read the modified call, but the tool ran with the model's
  arguments: a hook that redacted an argument by MODIFY sent the original
  to the handler anyway. The call now runs with the arguments the chain
  ended with, a MODIFY's or an in-place edit's, on every door (an AI
  channel, a realtime model, a reasoning backend, a conference, an external
  handler), validated again. A `metadata["arguments"]` rewrite keeps the
  last word, as before.

- **A transport that raises `asyncio.CancelledError` of its own is reported
  failed** (RFC 10.2, RMK-1041). A `deliver()` or an `on_event()` raising a
  `CancelledError` the transport met itself (a request another task
  cancelled, not the call's cancellation) left its target out of
  `delivery_results`, with no log line: the delivery set caught `Exception`
  only. The target now reads `failed`, code `CancelledError`, retryable, its
  message the exception's, and is logged as any failed send is; a failed
  `deliver()` counts against the circuit breaker, and a `retry_policy` does
  not retry it.
  - A cancellation aimed at the call ends it as before: its caller giving
    up, or the kit's close cutting the send (`kit_closed`).
  - An agent's turn ending cancelled is its turn's cut, never
    `InboundResult.error`, which a caller may raise.

- **A `kit.close()` while a cancelled task is still ending waits for it
  without spinning, and one called from that end returns** (RFC 12.10.4,
  RFC 23.3, RMK-1038). `cancel_task()` ends its task once the task's work
  has ended, its `on_complete` included. A `kit.close()` called from that
  `on_complete` never returned, the process at full CPU. A `kit.close()`
  while it ran kept a CPU busy until it was over: 1.9 s of CPU for a 2 s
  `on_complete`. The close now waits for that end idle, within its grace;
  one called from that end does not wait for the end it runs in, and
  returns once the kit is closed.

- **A `kit.close()` that joins a running one from the kit's own work no
  longer waits for that work or cuts it** (RFC 12.10.4, RMK-1019). The
  shutdown spared the work of a joining caller by its tasks only, never by
  the markers its first caller's code carried.
  - A tool whose turn the first close cut, closing the kit in its cleanup,
    had its close cut again by the turn executor's close; it now returns
    once the kit is closed.
  - A realtime model's tool call that the realtime channel's close cut,
    closing the kit in its cleanup, held that close 5 s; it now returns at
    once.
  - A `conference_started` handler closing the kit waited 5 s for the
    arrival callback it runs in, and 10 s when it joined another close; it
    now returns at once.
  - The turns a close runs under, the realtime call its handler serves, the
    conference activity and participant callback it runs inside are now read
    for every caller, and the waits read them again as a caller joins.
  - The model turn such a close runs in is cut all the same (RMK-1030), the
    call awaiting `close()` itself left to run; a call awaiting a close it
    started on a task of its own is cut with its turn.

- **A delivery placed in its room's idle lane is sent when the kit closes,
  whatever the store** (RFC 12.10.4, RMK-1039). A delivery waited in its
  lane from its placement until the lane, having read the room's delivery
  cursor, took it, and a close in that window dropped it as queued: a
  deferred `process_inbound` followed at once by `close()` lost its
  delivery on every store, and whether a close from elsewhere found it
  taken depended on how long the store took to read the cursor. A
  delivery placed while its lane is idle now runs from its
  placement: the close gives it its grace, and its call reads `kit_closed`
  with what it delivered. The lane is idle once the sends ahead have
  answered: an answer placed while their `AFTER_BROADCAST` hooks and
  responses run (a channel's response, a `send_event` from an
  `AFTER_BROADCAST` hook) is sent too, where it was stored and never
  delivered. One queued behind another is still dropped, and so is the one
  a lane kept when the close comes from that lane's own work (an
  `AFTER_BROADCAST` hook), which it could only run once the store is
  released. 0.110.0 is not affected.

- **An ASYNC hook's `close()` waits for the work that fired it**
  (RFC 12.10.4, RMK-1039). An observer started from a delivery lane's round
  or a turn counted as that work, so the close spared it: neither waited
  for nor cut. That work does not wait for its observer, so the close now
  waits for it and cuts it as any other, as roomkit-rs does. Before, the
  close could release the store under a lane still holding a delivery,
  whose rounds then failed over the closed store and whose call never
  returned.

- **`kit.close()` returns while calls keep arriving** (RMK-1016). The close
  waited for the work started after it began, and calls were taken until
  the store was sealed: with calls arriving with no gap, it had not returned
  after 20 s, and returned 7 s after the traffic stopped, 67,840 calls taken
  meanwhile. Calls are now refused from the close's start (above), and it
  returns with its 5 s grace.

- **`JevClassifier` sends its `model` with a client handed in** (RMK-1025).
  The model was used only when the classifier made its own client. A client
  passed in answered on its own default, so through a LiteLLM proxy the call
  named `jev-latest` and failed with a 400. The model now goes with every
  call.

- **The tools-already-used notes no longer send the model looking for
  `find_tools` when Tool Search is off** (RFC 6.4, RMK-1022). After a turn
  that called a tool, `AIChannel` adds a "Tools you've already used here"
  block to the next turn's notes. That block always said that more tools were
  hidden behind `find_tools` and that the model should search before saying
  it cannot do something. With Tool Search off, which is the case for any
  channel with a short tool list, the turn declares no `find_tools` and
  refuses a call to it. The block now says this only when the turn's Tool
  Search is on.

- **A `kit.close()` cancelled, or called while another runs, no longer
  leaves the kit half closed** (RFC 12.10.4, RMK-1015). The kit was marked
  closed on entry: a `close()` its caller cancelled (a timeout around it, a
  task cancelled while it closes) stopped where it stood, its channels never
  closed nor its store released, and every later `close()` returned at once;
  a second `close()` running beside the first returned before anything was
  closed. The kit now has one shutdown, run in a task of its own: every
  `close()` waits for it, a cancelled one cancels only its own wait, and the
  shutdown runs to its end while the event loop runs. A process that
  cancels every task as it ends (`asyncio.run` interrupted during its last
  `close()`) cuts the shutdown too: a later `close()` then raises
  `ShutdownCancelledError` (a `RoomKitError`) saying so. A `close()` from the kit's own work (a tool's
  call, a hook's body) still runs on once the shutdown has ended: the
  shutdown neither waits for it nor cuts it, whether that call started the
  shutdown or joined one under way. The model turn such a call runs in is
  cut all the same (RMK-1030), the call awaiting `close()` itself left to
  run; a call awaiting a close it started on a task of its own is cut with
  its turn.
- **A `kit.close()` from a delivery's hook, from a session's end, or from a
  discussion's `ON_SPEAK_QUEUE` hook returns and closes the kit**
  (RMK-1015). An ASYNC `AFTER_BROADCAST` hook runs in its room's delivery
  lane: a `kit.close()` from it waited for that lane, which waited for the
  hook, until the lane's 5 s grace ran out and its cancellation cut the
  close half way, the channels left open. A `voice_session_ended` handler
  that closes the kit after a client hung up waited for ever: a
  `RealtimeVoiceChannel`'s close waited for the teardown running the
  handler, and a `VoiceChannel`'s (as a `VideoChannel`'s and an
  `AVChannel`'s) for its own tasks, the handler's included. An ASYNC
  `ON_SPEAK_QUEUE` hook's close waited 5 s for the announcement running it.
  The close now spares the lane, the teardown, the announcement or the task
  it is called from: neither waited for nor cut, while every other channel
  closes and the kit is released; the deliveries queued behind a spared
  lane's are dropped, as any left at a close's end are. Two such calls at
  once (two sessions ending together), or one while another `close()` runs
  (a delegation's `on_complete` included), spare each one's work alike.

## [0.110.0] — 2026-10-27

### Added

- `AIChannel(serialize_room_turns=True)` (and `Agent`): the agent's turns in a
  room run one after the other, in the order its messages arrived (RFC §6.4,
  RMK-900). By default they run side by side, and the turn for a second task
  read the first one's order still unanswered, so it could do that task again.
  A turn takes its place when its message is delivered, starts once the one
  before it has written its answer (a cut one's kept text included), and
  reads the room as it is then, less what others wrote after its message:
  never a message that came after it, which waits its own turn, nor one
  deleted meanwhile. `kit.cancel_delivery(key)` on a waiting turn's delivery
  means it never starts; cutting the running turn lets the next one start. A
  message the running turn sends into its own room (a tool's
  `process_inbound`, `send_event` or `post`) that asks the same agent is
  answered after that turn: the call returns without waiting for the answer.
  A muted agent still reads each message as it comes, its answer withheld;
  one muted while its turn waits is withheld too, since a turn that waited is
  delivered on the room it starts in: a streaming client sees it begin once
  the turn before it has ended, and a hook judges its answer with the answer
  before it. Two such agents that ask each other from their running turns
  wait on each other until the tool's timeout (`tool_timeout_seconds`), and
  neither question is answered: only a message to the same agent is answered
  after its turn. The order is the room owner's, per process, as an ACP
  agent's is; a strategy that takes the agent's turns (`Loop`, `Supervisor`)
  orders them itself. The owner reads it from `Channel.serializes_room_turns`,
  which `ChannelDeclaration` carries for an agent built on an executor
  elsewhere. `examples/agent_turns_in_order.py` runs it.

- `LocalAudioBackend(output_latency_ms=...)`: the output latency the speaker
  asks PortAudio for, in milliseconds (RMK-554). The default (`None`) is
  unchanged: PortAudio's "low" with an `aec`, "high" without it, and "high"
  on macOS. A wider margin stops the underflows, heard as clicks, that a
  stalled Python callback causes: with an AEC, a C call holding the GIL for
  50 ms every 400 ms gave 84 underflows over three responses at "low" and
  none at 100 ms. It costs latency: a wider margin delays each response and
  each cut by as much. With an `aec`, the margin adds about as much to the
  echo delay (100 ms asked: echo at about 149 ms instead of 38); keep it
  inside the canceller's range: WebRTC about 500 ms in all, Speex its
  `filter_length` (200 ms by default). The AEC's echo delay can still drift
  under such stalls, more with the wider margin, and can let more echo
  through (RMK-973). A value that is not positive and finite raises
  `ValueError`. The `Speaker stream:` log line names the latency asked for
  (`latency=100ms`), and an echo delay past WebRTC's 500 ms, which the
  backend tells the AEC as 500, is now logged as a warning once per session.

- `gpt-6.1-terra` joins the OpenAI catalog: $1 / $5 per million, cached
  input $0.05, a $1.25 cache write, the 1.05M window and long-context rule
  (2x input and 1.5x output above 272k input tokens), and image input (its
  model and pricing pages, 2026-10-27). What Chat Completions does with its
  function tools is not checked on the wire yet: a turn with tools sends it no
  `reasoning_effort`, and nothing is refused before the request. The mirror's
  `gpt-6.1-terra-pro` is recorded in `check_models.py` as a route OpenAI does
  not document.

### Changed

- **BREAKING — `InMemoryStore` shares the rooms, bindings and participants it
  returns** (RFC §14.4, RMK-984). Every read made a deep copy of each record,
  21 reads per message to an agent: 17 % of a message's time. A room, a
  binding or a participant a read returns is now the store's snapshot, as an
  event already was: treat it as frozen and change it through a copy and a
  write, `await kit.store.update_room(room.model_copy(update={...}))`. A write
  copies its record in, so a change to the object passed to `create_room()`,
  `update_room()`, `add_binding()`, `update_binding()`, `add_participant()` or
  `update_participant()` no longer reaches the store, where until now it did.
  A message to an echo agent takes 2.15 ms instead of 2.60. What is shared:
  what `kit.get_room()`, `kit.store.get_binding()` and the other reads
  return, and the room, bindings and participants of the `RoomContext` a
  hook or a channel receives. Migration: a hook or a channel that changed its
  context's room or bindings in place, or code that changed a read record as
  a scratch copy, now changes the in-memory store behind the write
  interface's back: copy it with `model_copy(deep=True)` (a plain
  `model_copy()` shares its dicts), or change the room through the kit
  (`update_room_metadata()`). Code that changed a read record in place and
  then wrote it with `update_room()` still works, but not with
  `update_room_if()`, whose comparison then reads the changed value and
  refuses: write a copy. A custom store must now keep a caller's later change
  to the room, binding or participant it was written out of what it stores
  (copy it in, or serialize it), as for events. SQLiteStore and
  PostgresStore return a new object per read and are unchanged.

- **BREAKING — an agent's turn in the owner's process reads the request's
  events as they are** (RFC §10.6.1, §14.4, RMK-985). Each turn of an agent
  in the owner's process wrote its `TurnRequest` as JSON and parsed it back,
  383 µs for a request carrying 51 events of history, 87 % of it the
  history. The event the turn answers and the room's history are records
  nothing changes once made (committed events the store shares, or the
  owner's own for the turn), and now reach the executor as they are; the
  rest of the request (the room, the bindings, the binding, the notes) still
  crosses as JSON, so the executor changes its own copy of them. A message
  to an echo agent takes 1.75 ms instead of 2.19. This holds on any backend
  for a turn placed on an executor of the owner's process, Redis's local
  placement included; an executor reached across Redis still parses a copy.
  A value JSON has no form for, kept in an event's metadata, reaches an
  in-process executor as the object itself, where it read its text.
  Migration: a channel's `on_event()` or an executor's hook that changed its
  event or a history event in place (`event.metadata["x"] = ...`) now changes
  the owner's object, and on `InMemoryStore` the stored record: copy it first
  (`event.model_copy(update=...)`), as RFC §14.4 always asked.

### Fixed

- **A queued delivery is made by the caller that queued it** (RFC §8.3, §22.2,
  RMK-983). A `Queued` strategy shared by several callers (the kit's
  `delivery_strategy="queued"`) delivered every caller's request from the
  first caller's drain, inside that caller's work: an application's message at
  depth 0, queued while a hook delivered from work 3 deep, was stored 3 deep,
  and at the limit no agent was asked; a voice text queued behind a
  hook-injected one entered silently. The caller that drains now delivers the
  batch its own request heads, then hands the drain to the caller whose
  request heads the queue, which delivers that batch in its own task, with its
  own depth, frames and room lock: a locked hook that drains no longer leaves
  the callers behind it waiting on the lock it holds. A caller cancelled while
  it waits withdraws its request, and hands on a drain it was handed; a caller
  cancelled while it drains hands the drain on too, where every caller behind
  it was cancelled; a caller whose request its batch carried, cut while it
  was sent, receives `unknown` (`strategy_outcome_unknown`), where it
  received `CancelledError`: the batch may or may not have reached the
  channel. A wait for idle longer than
  `playback_timeout` delivers the batch anyway, as `WaitForIdle`'s does, where
  it failed `strategy_failed`.

- **A caller holding a room's lock delivers past a queue another caller
  drains** (RFC §9.5.1, §22.2, RMK-997). A locked hook (a SYNC
  `BEFORE_BROADCAST`) that delivered, into its room or another one, through
  a shared `Queued` strategy while another caller drained it waited behind a
  batch whose delivery needed the lock the hook held: both ended at
  `process_timeout`, the hook's message refused, nothing written. So did a
  hook delivering from the very message the kit-wide strategy
  (`delivery_strategy="queued"`, one queue for every room) was delivering.
  Such a caller now delivers at once, unbatched, as `Immediate` does: it is
  nested in the section that holds the lock, which a batch cannot wait on. A
  caller holding a lock that finds no drain under way drains as before.

- **`find_tools` finds a tool asked for by its name** (RMK-993). A query
  that is a tool's name returns that tool first, compared without case;
  until now it was scored among the tools sharing its words, and an untagged
  tool came after every tagged tool of a source that carried the same words
  in its name and again in its tags (15th of 686 in one catalogue, behind
  the search and send tools of two mail sources). A query word now counts
  once per tool, from the strongest field that carries it: the name (×3),
  else the tags (×2, was ×3), plus the description (×1); a word in both the
  name and the tags counted twice. A tag stays above the description, as
  the cross-lingual bridge, and below the name, since a source tags every
  tool it serves with the same words.

- **A realtime session that ended keeps no transcription state** (RMK-983). A
  transcription the provider handed on once the channel ended its session, or
  while a start that then failed was running, left the session's answer depth
  and its ordering lock behind for good, one of each per call that ended so: a
  slow leak on a server that takes many calls. Such a transcription was
  already dropped, its room gone; now nothing of it is kept, and a start that
  fails forgets what was transcribed and when the user's turn began, as a
  session's end does. An `ON_TRANSCRIPTION` hook still running as the session
  ends, and an injection the provider still held, no longer write the
  session's last text or its depth back after it; on a conference, whose room
  outlives its session, an injection held across a reconnect no longer moves
  the new session's next answer. A start that fails also forgets its barge-in
  state. The last words a provider hands on as its connection drops are still
  recorded: the session is its room's until the channel ends it.

- **A channel's `metadata_updates` are written on the room** (RFC §10.1 step
  15, RMK-976). The core collected them in `BroadcastResult.metadata_updates`
  and never wrote them, and dropped a transport's `deliver()` ones: a
  transport returning `{"crm_contact": "c_42"}` left the room's metadata
  without it, on every store. The updates of `on_event()` and `deliver()`
  are now merged key by key in the order the targets answered and written
  once per delivery set, a partial update under the room lock, before
  `AFTER_BROADCAST`. A key only the framework writes, under `roomkit:` or of
  the room's private state (`author_register`, `_speak_queue_results`), is
  dropped with a warning naming the channel, the rest applied.

- **BREAKING — `send_event()` refuses a channel the kit does not register**
  (RFC §10.5, RMK-977). A channel never registered raised
  `ChannelNotFoundError`, as a channel the room does not bind does, and one
  the room still bound after `unregister_channel()` wrote and delivered the
  event. Both now raise `ChannelNotRegisteredError` before anything is read,
  nothing written. `post()` already refused an unregistered host channel so,
  and `commit_event()`, whose record reaches no one, takes any source as
  before. A task's posted result, the agent's message, is still committed
  from a process that does not register the agent (RFC §19.7.5 rule 19).
  Migration: a caller that caught `ChannelNotFoundError` for an unknown
  channel catches `ChannelNotRegisteredError` too, or `RoomKitError`.

### Security

- **BREAKING — an agent's answer text is published only for a delegated
  task's trace** (RFC §6.4, §23.3 step 5, RMK-972). In 0.109.0, with
  `AIChannel(publish_text_deltas=True)`, every turn of the agent published
  its text as `TEXT_DELTA`, which `BEFORE_BROADCAST` never judges: a room
  subscriber read the whole of an answer a hook blocked or redacted, in a
  room, in a task's child room a transport is shared into, and for a turn
  another agent's message starts in a task's child room. The room's owner
  now publishes a turn's `TEXT_DELTA` only while the delegation reads that
  turn as its trace, the rows a child room with no shared transport stores
  without a hook (RFC §23.3 step 5); any other turn's is dropped, and so is
  one an executor publishes after its turn or outside one. A task's text is
  published as before: the same windows, `round`, and order before a
  round's tool-call events. A dashboard that read a room's text reads its
  stored messages, or a streaming transport's live pipe, instead. A host
  that filters or redacts answers may now turn the option on, once every
  process that owns rooms runs this release: the owner decides, and one on
  0.109.0 still publishes every turn's text. What is published is the
  trace's text, which no hook judges either; a delegation cut short may
  store less of it than was published, the text its executor read ahead of
  the reader.

- **A room's private-state keys are the runtime's alone in its metadata**
  (RFC §14.1, §10.1 step 12, RMK-978). A register of authors the room's
  metadata held under `author_register` was merged into the store's at the
  room's next named turn, whoever wrote it: an integrator's caller who could
  write the metadata planted a register giving its own source rank 1 under
  another sender's name, so its messages read `Alice` and the real Alice
  read `Alice (2)`. `create_room(metadata=...)` and `update_room_metadata()`,
  from a hook's body too, and a turn's `TurnHost.update_room_metadata`, now
  drop a key of the room's private state (`author_register`,
  `_speak_queue_results`) with a warning naming the call, and write the rest,
  as a channel's `metadata_updates` do: the forged register never lands, and
  a read-modify-write of a room from before 0.109 that still holds one
  writes. The merge stays, for a room stored before and a process of an
  earlier release, which only the runtime can still write.

- **Every `roomkit:` key of a room's metadata is the framework's alone**
  (RFC §5.1, §7.5 rule 7, RMK-978). `create_room(metadata=...)` and
  `update_room_metadata()` refused only `roomkit:channel_state:` keys: an
  integrator's caller who could write the metadata cleared a detach's
  revocation (`roomkit:detached_channels`), and the next message on the
  detached channel attached it again and was delivered, as a post from a
  detached host channel was. Every writer the kit takes a room's metadata
  from (those two calls, from a hook's body too, a turn's
  `TurnHost.update_room_metadata`, a channel's `metadata_updates`) now drops
  any `roomkit:` key with a warning naming it, and writes the rest:
  `roomkit:channel_state:`, which raised `ValueError`, is dropped too. So a
  read-modify-write (`update_room_metadata(r, {**room.metadata, ...})`,
  `create_room(metadata=room.metadata)`) writes in a room that saw a detach,
  and leaves the revocation as it is; only `attach_channel()` grants a
  detached channel back. The framework writes these keys through the store,
  which takes any key. An application that kept its own value under a
  `roomkit:` key renames it.

- **`update_event()` keeps the record of the author the event was committed
  with** (RFC §10.1 step 12, RMK-978). It stored the caller's
  `metadata["author"]` as given: an update naming another author at rank 1
  made a reader, and a register rebuilt from the timeline, trust it, where a
  message, `send_event()`, a hook's injection and `commit_event()` drop such
  a record. The update now keeps the record the event was committed with,
  whether its metadata names another or none, and writes none on an event
  committed with none: `update_event(..., metadata={})` now clears every key
  but that record, which it keeps.

- **A task a locked hook left running calls into the room as a new arrival
  once the hook is over** (RFC §9.5.1, §13.5, RMK-978). The task kept the
  room lock's lease while the event's pass held the lock, so a call it made
  after the hook had returned, while the pass ran its next hook, was adopted
  as the hook's own: it committed ahead of the event, under a lock nothing
  held for it, and ran its hooks there. A hook's body now has the room locks
  lent to it only while it runs: a task it starts acts for it until it
  returns, awaited or not, and its later calls wait for the lock and commit
  after the event. Such a call is an ordinary arrival, neither refused nor
  adopted: a later hook of the same pass that awaits the task waits for the
  lock its pass holds, until its own timeout, which cancels the task it
  awaited unless it shields it. Await work in the hook that starts it. An
  off-lock hook's body is held to the same rule: a task it starts stands in
  the event's admission order only while the body runs, and its call once
  the body has returned, while the check's next hook runs, takes a ticket and
  commits after the event, where it was adopted ahead of it.

- **An ASYNC hook on a SYNC trigger draws on the cascade's hook calls**
  (RFC §9.5.1, §10.1 step 16, RMK-978). An observer of a SYNC trigger ran
  as work of its own: an ASYNC `BEFORE_BROADCAST` hook that called
  `send_event()` into its room on every event never stopped, each post firing
  it again on a budget of its own (more than 5,000 calls in 8 s, and
  `process_inbound()` never returned). Fired from the room's work (a pass's
  section, an event's admission work, a delivery set's work), an observer's
  body is now that cascade's work, as an `AFTER_BROADCAST` body is: a call it
  makes into the room is a new arrival that draws one of the cascade's hook
  calls, at least one deeper than its event, and past the cap it is refused
  as theirs are (`send_event()` and `post()` store it `BLOCKED` with
  `reentry_loop_cap`). So do the observers of `BEFORE_BROADCAST`,
  `BEFORE_DELIVER`, `BEFORE_TTS`, `BEFORE_AI_CONTEXT_BUILD`,
  `BEFORE_AI_GENERATION`, `ON_SPEAK_DECISION`, `ON_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` and
  the other SYNC triggers that fire once per event. The triggers that fire
  per tool call, per round or per input request (`BEFORE_TOOL_USE`,
  `ON_TOOL_CALL`, `AFTER_TOOL_ROUND`, `ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED`) keep the budget
  they had: their observers run as any task the turn's work starts, so a
  post they make while the turn's delivery runs draws one of the cascade's
  passes and stops at `10 × max_chain_depth`, and a direct change
  (`update_event()`, a progress card) draws nothing. What they send is now at
  least as deep as the turn was when the trigger fired, once the turn is over
  too, where a post made after the turn started at depth 0. Behaviour change:
  the observer of a per-event trigger makes its calls one deeper than the
  event it observes, where they started at depth 0, so with
  `max_chain_depth=2` an agent no longer answers the follow-up an observer
  posts on a person's message. Migration: raise `max_chain_depth`.

- **A speech-to-speech model's loop with a hook ends at `max_chain_depth`**
  (RFC §8.3, §9.5.1, §12.4, RMK-983). An ASYNC `ON_TOOL_CALL` or
  `BEFORE_TOOL_USE` hook that posted into the room at each call of a realtime
  model (a `RealtimeVoiceChannel`, a conference's realtime configuration) made
  it answer and call again without end: the hooks fired outside the call's
  context, so each post started at depth 0, and the channel injected a text
  into its model at any depth. So did a hook on the model's words
  (`ON_TRANSCRIPTION`, `ON_PARTIAL_TRANSCRIPTION`) that told it something at
  each of its answers. A realtime or conference tool call's gate, handler and
  reports, the observers they fire included (a call the session's end cuts,
  one a reasoning backend's own provider serves), now make their calls into a
  room at least as deep as the model's answer that issued the call, read as
  the call arrives; a `RealtimeVoiceChannel`'s transcription hooks run at the
  depth of the answer they hear, and their ASYNC observers keep it once the
  words were processed, as a tool call's observers do; and a text whose answer
  would be past the limit (its depth plus one reaching `max_chain_depth`)
  enters the model's session silently, whatever brings it: a broadcast,
  `deliver()`, a pipeline's handoff greeting, or `inject_text()`, whose text
  is at least as deep as the work it is called from (a turn, a tool call, a
  hook's body), as `deliver()`'s is, whatever `chain_depth` it names, so a
  hook that injects at each call ends too. The model takes it into its context
  and answers nothing, as an agent past the limit is not asked, and the log
  says why. With `max_chain_depth=4` the loop ends after three posts.
  Behaviour change: in a room with a realtime model and an agent, their
  exchange ends at the limit one turn sooner, as between two agents, a handoff
  greeting at the limit no longer makes the new agent speak. Migration: raise
  `max_chain_depth`. Example: `examples/realtime_tool_observer_depth.py`.

- **A hook that asks an agent again from its body ends at `max_chain_depth`,
  and a task it starts begins a new chain** (RFC §8.3, §9.5.1, RMK-1004). An
  ASYNC hook on a turn's trigger (`BEFORE_AI_GENERATION`, `ON_AI_RESPONSE`...)
  observes no event of a depth of its own: posting from its body once the
  turn was over, it posted at depth 1 every time, so a hook that reminded the
  agent of a rule after each turn made it answer 51 times, until the reentry
  cap. And a task such a hook started began a new chain only if the turn was
  over when it sent: a quality gate relaunching the agent from a task while a
  slower observer of the same answer still ran (the turn waits for them) sent
  at the turn's depth, one deeper each round, and its fifth relaunch was never
  answered. The body of a hook run asynchronously (an ASYNC hook, and a hook
  registered SYNC on an ASYNC trigger, which runs as its ASYNC hooks do) now
  sends at least as deep as the work that fired it was when its trigger
  fired (a turn, a tool call, a model's answer), for as long as the body
  runs, that work over or not, a `TurnHost` verb from a turn executor's hook
  included; a task it starts that calls once the body returned begins at
  depth 0, whether the turn or the trigger's other hooks still run or not
  (its budget is unchanged: the room delivery's while that delivery runs).
  The reminder loop ends after four answers at `max_chain_depth=5`. Behaviour
  change, both ways: a post from the body of a turn trigger's hook made once
  the turn is over is as deep as the turn's response, so the agent no longer
  answers one made at the limit; and a task such a body started, calling
  while the turn or a sibling hook still runs, is at depth 0 where it was at
  the turn's depth, so the agent answers it at the limit too, and a loop
  through such tasks ends at the reentry cap or by the hook's own count, not
  at `max_chain_depth`. Migration: send from a task the hook starts what must
  begin a new chain, pass `chain_depth=` from that task to continue one, or
  raise `max_chain_depth`. Example: `examples/hook_observer_depth.py`.

- **A hook on what a voice agent says, or on a realtime model's delegation,
  ends at `max_chain_depth`** (RFC §8.3, §12.2, §12.4.1, RMK-998). A hook on
  what an agent speaking through text to speech says (`BEFORE_TTS`, on each
  sentence of a streamed reply too, and `AFTER_TTS`), on a `VoiceChannel` or
  a conference's voice lane, ran at depth 0: one that asked the agent
  something after each of its answers ran until the reentry cap (41 answers
  at `max_chain_depth=4`), never the depth limit. So did a hook on a
  speech-to-speech model's delegation (`ON_REALTIME_DELEGATION`), on a
  `RealtimeVoiceChannel` and in a conference. These hooks now run at the
  depth of the answer they speak or that delegated, read as it arrives, as a
  realtime tool call's do: the loop ends after three answers at
  `max_chain_depth=4`. `VoiceChannel.say()` is unchanged: its hooks run at
  the depth of the code that calls it. `ON_OUTPUT_AUDIO_LEVEL` is unchanged:
  it fires per audio frame, for no answer in particular. Behaviour change: a
  post from such a hook is as deep as the answer, so the agent no longer
  answers one made at the limit. Migration: raise `max_chain_depth`.
  Examples: `examples/hook_observer_depth.py`,
  `examples/realtime_tool_observer_depth.py`.

## [0.109.0] — 2026-10-25

### Added

- `MCPToolProvider(label=...)`, also on `from_url` and `from_command`: the
  host's name for the server, the `<server>` of an MCP alias
  `mcp__<server>__<tool>` (RFC §21.2, RMK-493). Letters, digits and `_ . -`,
  64 at most, no `__` and no final `_`, either of which would make an alias
  read another server; anything else raises `ValueError`. Optional: see
  Security for what it changes. `examples/mcp_server_labels.py` composes two
  labelled servers, their tools declared under their aliases, under a policy
  that keeps one out.

- **A room's private state in the store** (RFC §14.1, RMK-631):
  `ConversationStore.get_private_state(room_id, key)` and
  `set_private_state(room_id, key, value)` keep what a room holds for the
  runtime alone, a JSON object per key, apart from the room's metadata,
  which `get_room()` returns and clients may read. A read is the caller's own
  copy, `None` for an unknown room or key; a write is made under the room
  lock the caller holds, writes nothing for a room the store lacks, removes
  the key when the value is `None`, and removes the copy the room's metadata
  may still hold under the key in the same write, so a key moves out of the
  metadata in one step; the room's deletion takes its private state. The
  keys are the implementation's, and each reserves the same key in the
  room's metadata, where the base class keeps it and from which `set`
  removes the copy. `InMemoryStore`, `SQLiteStore` (table `private_state`,
  schema 12) and `PostgresStore` (table `private_state`, rows of a room
  deleted with it) keep it apart. The room's register of authors is its
  first key (see Security). A custom store keeps working: the base class
  keeps each key in the room's metadata, as before, and warns once per
  store that it is readable there.

- **An agent's answer text, published live as `TEXT_DELTA`, when the host
  turns it on** (RFC §6.4, RMK-951). The live pipe reaches only a room's
  streaming transports, and a delegated turn's text, collected for its
  result, reached no one until the turn ended, while its tool calls were
  already published live in the child room. With the new keyword-only
  `AIChannel(publish_text_deltas=True)`, `AIChannel` publishes its answer's
  text as `EphemeralEventType.TEXT_DELTA` ephemerals (`text`, `round`,
  `channel_id`) in the room it speaks in, child rooms included, coalesced
  on the new `AIChannel(text_coalesce_ms=80, text_coalesce_chars=256)`,
  flushed before a round's tool-call events. It is off by default: nothing
  is published, and the coalescing settings have no effect.
  `BEFORE_BROADCAST` does not cover this stream (see Security).
  Like every turn ephemeral, it reaches no one the answer would not reach
  (RFC §8.4). A 400-token answer takes 13 publishes; the cost is within 0.3 %
  of a turn.
  Rolling upgrade: a 0.108.0 process cannot parse a `text_delta` event
  (`EphemeralEvent.from_dict` raises `ValueError`): an owner logs an error
  for each one a newer executor sends and publishes none, and the Redis
  realtime backend drops it with a warning. Turn the option on only once
  every worker runs 0.109.0.

- **A test catches a public signature change that can break a caller.**
  `tests/public_api_signatures.json` holds the signatures of the classes and
  functions the packages export (1 080 objects, 6 173 members): parameters and
  their defaults, sync or async, properties, enum values. `test_public_api.py`
  fails on a name, member or parameter removed or renamed, a parameter made
  required or moved, a default changed, a method made async or an enum value
  changed; an addition passes and needs no entry. The commit that breaks a
  signature on purpose runs `make api-snapshot` and carries its BREAKING
  entry. Type annotations, what a call does, and the hooks pydantic calls
  on a model (`model_post_init`) are not compared.

- **One rule says which import paths are public** (RMK-948). A name is
  public when the `__all__` of `roomkit` or of one of its packages lists it,
  imported from that package; a module path (`roomkit.voice.stt.deepgram`)
  is internal and may move, an underscore name is internal everywhere
  (README, "Public API"; the docs site's Public API page says how a break is
  announced). 172 names that examples, the docs, the API reference or
  applications use were in no `__all__` and are now exported, each from
  its package, so the API guards pin them (149 classes and functions, 23
  constants and type aliases), among them every STT and TTS provider and
  its config from `roomkit.voice.stt` / `roomkit.voice.tts` (new `__all__` for
  `roomkit.voice.stt`), the voice and video backends from
  `roomkit.voice.backends` / `roomkit.video.backends` (new `__all__` for
  both), the realtime transports from `roomkit.voice.realtime`, the
  realtime providers of OpenAI, Gemini, xAI and ElevenLabs from their
  packages, `IdentityResolver` and `MockIdentityResolver` from
  `roomkit.identity`, `validate_public_url` from `roomkit.providers`, the
  steering directives, `LoopEndMarker`, `STANDALONE` and `TURNS_KEY` from
  `roomkit.models`, the status bus and tool-audit families from
  `roomkit.orchestration`, `PostgresSchemaError` and the Postgres schema
  (`POSTGRES_SCHEMA`, `POSTGRES_SCHEMA_VERSION`) from `roomkit.store`,
  `fence` and `turn_report_claim` from `roomkit.tools`, and others.
  Gemini's transcript types and Qwen3's clone reference are exported under
  vendor names (`GeminiTranscript`, `GeminiTranscriptWord`,
  `GeminiTranscriptSegment`, `Qwen3VoiceCloneConfig`). Among those the API
  reference documented: `InboundRoomRouter`,
  `DefaultInboundRoomRouter` and `DeliveryContext` from `roomkit`,
  `build_handoff_tool`, `RCSDeliveryResult`, the Buzz and Discord parsers
  from `roomkit.sources`, the Meta, Azure MAI, Voxtral, Azure Speech and
  Fish Audio errors from `roomkit.voice.stt` / `roomkit.voice.tts`,
  `MockVoiceCall`, `TwilioWebSocketBackend` and `AuthCallback`. Among
  those an application holds or writes: `HookEngine` (what
  `kit.hook_engine` is) and `HookRegistration` (what `add_room_hook()`
  returns) from `roomkit`, `room_tasks` from `roomkit.tasks`, and
  `compose`, `addressed` and `judgments_of`, the building blocks of a custom
  speak policy, from `roomkit.speaking`. `roomkit.channels` gets an
  `__all__` listing the channels and factories it already held. A name whose
  module `import roomkit` did not load is exported lazily: `import roomkit`
  loads no new module, a missing extra raises its own error on first use
  (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'httpx'`), `dir()`, `help()` and
  `inspect.getmembers()` list only what the package has bound and never
  import a lazy name (a missing extra cannot fail them), and a type checker
  reads the real class and reports a name the package does not export.
  Every module path that imported keeps importing (see Changed for what that
  path now promises); the `roomkit.voice.get_*()` lookups keep working and
  are internal. `tests/test_public_imports.py` fails on an example, a
  document or a docstring under `src/` that imports a roomkit name from
  anywhere else, and `make docs` runs the same check on the docs site.

- `kit.post()` and `HostChannel` (exported from `roomkit` and
  `roomkit.channels`): the host writes to a room's people in its own name
  (RFC §10.5, RMK-947). A notice, a workflow's question, a reminder
  is the application's words, not an agent's: it comes from a transport of
  type `HOST` (new `ChannelType.HOST`), never delivered to, so the room reads
  it as a party's message and broadcasts it to its transports. `post()`
  registers the host channel under `"host"` on first use (`ValueError` when
  another type holds the id), solicits no agent unless `addressed_to` names
  one, signs with `participant_id` and keeps `metadata`. The speaker is a
  participant the host channel reaches, by their id or their identity's,
  as a turn's sender is read (RMK-954): `kit.add_member(room_id, "host",
  "desk")` makes a member one, and any other id (nobody's, a member
  reached through SMS only, an agent channel's) raises
  `ParticipantNotFoundError` before anything is written, the first post's
  attach included. `chain_depth=` names the chain the post continues, as
  `send_event()`'s does (RMK-954). `channel_id=` speaks from another
  registered `HostChannel`, and `organization_id=` refuses another
  organization's room with `RoomNotFoundError` (RFC §17.2).
  `idempotency_key=` makes a replay return the event its key committed,
  texting nothing again, read before the reentry budget from the room's own
  work; a blank key is no key. A room that never bound the host channel gets
  it attached on its first post, in one section under the room lock:
  concurrent first posts attach it once, and a binding the integrator sets,
  before or concurrently, keeps its settings. One `process_timeout` bounds
  the whole call, the wait for that lock included (`ProcessTimeoutError`),
  and once the lock is held the attach runs to its end, a cancelled
  caller's included, and stays when the deadline passes during it, the
  message then not written. A room the host channel was detached from is
  refused with `ChannelNotFoundError`, a closed or archived room with
  `RoomClosedError`, and an argument `send_event()` refuses before the
  attach, each with nothing written. A host channel attached as
  `INTELLIGENCE` raises `ValueError` before anything is written, and
  `process_inbound()` on it before anything is read. It declares every media
  type, and narrows nothing an agent's answer may carry (see "an agent's
  answer is narrowed only by the transports that send"). An intelligence
  channel used for this was refused by a Discussion room and turned the
  host's words into an agent's output; a `SYSTEM` source dropped the author.
  `deliver()` remains the way in for the room's agents.
  `examples/host_post.py` texts a customer from a shop's backend.
  Rolling upgrade: a version before this one cannot read a stored `"host"`
  channel type. Its store reads of the room's bindings and events raise
  `ValidationError` once a post wrote one, so every worker sharing a store
  must run this version before any of them posts.

- **A session's video recording can be encrypted at rest** (RFC §17.6,
  RMK-568). `VideoRecordingConfig` had no encryption setting, so
  `PyAVVideoRecorder` and `OpenCVVideoRecorder` wrote a session's video in
  the clear with no way to configure otherwise. It now takes `encryption`,
  a `RecordingEncryption` (from `roomkit.voice.pipeline`), and
  `storage_encrypted_at_rest`, the fields `RecordingConfig` and
  `MediaRecordingConfig` already carry. With `encryption`, each finished
  file goes through the cipher's `encrypt_file()` at `stop()`, and at
  `close()` for a recording still open: the result's `url` and
  `size_bytes` are the encrypted artifact's and `metadata["encryption"]`
  names the cipher, and a file the cipher cannot encrypt is deleted. A file
  whose flush or close raises is encrypted all the same before the error
  propagates, and `close()` logs a recording that fails and goes on with
  the next. With `storage_encrypted_at_rest=True` and no `encryption`, the
  file stays as written and `metadata["encryption"]` is `"storage"`. With
  neither, the recording is written unencrypted, as before: unlike the
  audio and room recorders, the video recorders do not refuse to start
  (see Security for `VideoChannel`). `examples/pyav_video_recorder.py
  --encrypt` stores its MP4 encrypted.

### Changed

- **BREAKING — the kit's room hook verbs and `claim_room_strategy()` are
  async and take the organization the caller acts for** (RFC §17.2,
  RMK-487). They were synchronous and read no room: a tenant's host that
  knew another tenant's room id could add a room hook there and read every
  message it broadcast, remove or disable that room's hooks (its
  moderation among them), enable a hook name for its turns, or probe
  whether it held a strategy. `add_room_hook()`, `remove_room_hook()`,
  `enable_room_hook()`, `disable_room_hook()` and `claim_room_strategy()`
  are now coroutines with `organization_id=None` (keyword-only): with one,
  the room is read first, and another organization's room raises
  `RoomNotFoundError` with nothing registered, removed, enabled, disabled
  or claimed. Unset, no room is read, as before. `kit.hook_engine`'s
  `add_room_hook()` / `remove_room_hook()` and the turn client's
  `enable_room_hook()` / `disable_room_hook()` stay synchronous: they hold
  no store and are the trusted level below the kit's calls.
  Migrate: `await` the five calls,
  `await kit.add_room_hook(room_id, trigger, execution, fn, ...)`,
  `await kit.remove_room_hook(room_id, name)`,
  `await kit.enable_room_hook(room_id, name)`,
  `await kit.disable_room_hook(room_id, name)`, and in a strategy's own
  `install()`, `await kit.claim_room_strategy(room_id, self)`; a host
  serving several organizations passes `organization_id=`. A test whose
  kit is a `MagicMock` and installs a built-in strategy gives it
  `kit.claim_room_strategy = AsyncMock()`.

- **BREAKING — a name is public only where a package's `__all__` lists
  it, and `__all__` decides what a star import binds** (RMK-948). A module
  path (`roomkit.voice.stt.deepgram`, `roomkit.models.event`) is internal
  even when it holds a public name: it keeps importing in this release, and
  may move or be renamed in any release (README, "Public API"; see Added
  for the rule and the names now exported).
  `from roomkit.channels import *` binds 37 names where it bound 62: no
  longer `ChannelType`, `ChannelCapabilities`, `ChannelMediaType` or the
  eleven `*_CAPABILITIES` constants, and
  `from roomkit.video.backends import *` no longer binds its five `get_*()`
  lookups; each still imports by name. `roomkit.sources` no
  longer holds `typing.Any`. A star import resolves every name `__all__`
  lists, the lazy ones included: on a core install,
  `from roomkit.voice.tts import *`, `roomkit.voice.realtime` and
  `roomkit.video.avatar` need the extras of the providers they list
  (httpx, fastapi, numpy), as `from roomkit.voice import *` already did, and
  `from roomkit.voice.realtime import *` needs fastapi even with the `dev`
  extra. The attribute `roomkit.tools.fence` is now the function `fence`,
  not the submodule, and so is what `import roomkit.tools.fence as m` binds;
  `from roomkit.tools.fence import named_blocks` still works.
  Migrate: import every roomkit name from the package whose `__all__` lists
  it (`from roomkit.voice.stt import DeepgramSTTProvider`, not
  `from roomkit.voice.stt.deepgram import DeepgramSTTProvider`); a name a
  star import no longer binds is imported by name from its package
  (`from roomkit.models import ChannelType`), and `Any` from `typing`;
  `from roomkit.tools import fence, named_blocks` replaces the submodule;
  a star import of `roomkit.voice.tts`, `roomkit.voice.realtime` or
  `roomkit.video.avatar` on a core install names what it uses, or installs
  those extras.

- **BREAKING — what an ASYNC hook sends into its room, and the
  `update_event()`, `delete_event()` and `regenerate_response()` it makes
  there, stop at the reentry cap of the cascade that fired it, and are one
  deeper than the event that fired it** (RFC §8.3, §9.5.1, §10.1 step 16,
  §10.3, §19.7.5, RMK-954). An `AFTER_BROADCAST` hook, and a change's
  `ON_EVENT_UPDATED` or `ON_EVENT_DELETED` hook, runs once the event's
  delivery set has run, and each call it made into its room was a new
  arrival with a budget of its own, at depth 0: a hook that posted after
  every event, its own posts included, looped without bound (2,000 posts in
  3.9 s; with an agent answering each post, 1,000 model calls), and so did
  one that updated, deleted or regenerated on every change, in a Discussion
  room too (200 runs when it was stopped).
  Each cascade now keeps two counters of `10 × max_chain_depth`: its own
  passes (its answers, chained streams and injected events) and, apart, the
  calls of all its ASYNC hooks' bodies together. While a hook's body runs, a
  call it makes into its room, or a message it sends that opens a room,
  draws one hook call: past the cap, `send_event()` and `post()` store the
  event `BLOCKED` with `reentry_loop_cap`, no hook run, and return it, and
  `process_inbound()` returns `blocked=True, reason="reentry_loop_cap"`. A
  direct `update_event()`, `delete_event()` or `regenerate_response()` made
  from a hook's body draws one hook call too, and past the cap raises the
  new `ReentryLoopCapError` (exported from `roomkit`), nothing written; an
  error the body lets escape is logged as a warning. A direct change's own
  hooks run on the budget of the work it is made in, one of their own from
  outside it.
  A call a hook's body makes, into whatever room, is also at least one
  deeper than the event that fired the hook, as a call made within a turn
  is at least as deep as its response: a `post()`, a `send_event()`, a
  `deliver()` (a queued item carries the depth), a message, a regeneration.
  `deliver()` now takes that floor in a turn or a tool call too, queued
  included: an item a tool handler queues carries the turn's depth, where it
  carried the `chain_depth` passed, 0 by default.
  A hook that asks an agent again after each of its answers therefore ends
  at `max_chain_depth`, or at a discussion's `max_depth`, whose turns each
  have a budget of their own: about `max_chain_depth / 2` answers (2 at the
  default limit of 5, 3 at 6), where it looped.
  A notice costs the agents no answer and their answers block no notice: a
  hook that posts once per event draws one hook call per event, and a
  notice is blocked only past `10 × max_chain_depth` calls of all the
  cascade's hooks together. A task the body starts and does not await,
  calling once the body has returned, is work of its own: depth 0 and a
  budget of its own.
  Who meets it: a hook that asks an agent again after each of its answers
  (a judge), and a hook whose calls into its room, or whose direct changes,
  take more than `10 × max_chain_depth` hook calls (50 by default) in one
  cascade, all its hooks together: a hook that edits, deletes or
  regenerates on every change, bulk work from one body (15 deletes against
